edges.description: Intracellular bacterial persistence drives a chronic macrophage- and plasma-cell-rich inflammatory reaction.
Persistent granulomatous inflammation and granulation tissue produce the enlarging genital ulcers that define the disease.
Chronic scarring inflammation can obstruct lymphatic drainage of the genital region.
Granuloma inguinale presents with chronic genital ulcers.
Long-standing donovanosis lesions can undergo malignant transformation to squamous cell carcinoma.
The chronic bleeding genital ulcer acts as a cofactor for HIV transmission and acquisition.

nodes.description: Azithromycin is the recommended oral macrolide therapy for donovanosis and is continued once weekly until lesions have completely healed.

evidence.reference_title: European guideline for the management of donovanosis, 2010.
evidence.snippet: The recommended treatment is azithromycin 1 g weekly until complete healing is achieved.
Azithromycin has emerged as the drug of choice and should be used if the diagnosis is confirmed or suspected.

nodes.description: K. granulomatis depends on bacterial 70S-ribosome translation. The principal donovanosis antibiotics, including azithromycin, erythromycin, and doxycycline, act through bacterial ribosomal targets and must be continued long enough to clear the chronic intracellular infection.

nodes.description: Genital papules enlarge into chronic ulcerogranulomatous, hypertrophic, necrotic, or sclerotic lesions; the ulcerogranulomatous phenotype predominates and produces the beefy, friable genital ulcer typical of donovanosis.

evidence.snippet: The incubation period is approximately 50 days with genital papules developing into ulcers that increase in size.

evidence.reference_title: Clinico-epidemiological study of donovanosis in Durban, South Africa.
evidence.snippet: Lesions were ulcero-granulomatous in 162, hypertrophic in eight and necrotic in one.

nodes.description: Doxycycline is an oral tetracycline alternative for donovanosis, used as a prolonged ribosome-targeting antibacterial regimen until lesions heal.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of genital ulcers.
evidence.snippet: Lymphogranuloma venereum and donovanosis are treated with 21 days of oral doxycycline.

nodes.description: Donovanosis genital ulcers bleed readily and are a recognized risk factor for HIV transmission and acquisition, and treatment failure can occur in advanced HIV disease.

evidence.reference_title: Global eradication of donovanosis: an opportunity for limiting the spread of HIV-1 infection.
evidence.snippet: Donovanosis is an uncommon GUD with low infectivity characterised by large ulcers that bleed readily and has been identified as a risk factor for HIV in men in Durban, South Africa.

nodes.description: Granuloma inguinale causes genital papules that become progressively enlarging chronic ulcers, most often of the ulcerogranulomatous type.

evidence.snippet: Four types of lesions are described - ulcerogranulomatous, hypertrophic, necrotic and sclerotic.

nodes.description: K. granulomatis persists in genital tissue biopsy specimens predominantly inside variably sized cytoplasmic vacuoles of macrophages, corresponding to the intracytoplasmic Donovan bodies used for diagnosis.

evidence.reference_title: Ultrastructure of Calymmatobacterium granulomatis: comparison of culture with tissue biopsy specimens.
evidence.snippet: In tissue specimens the bacteria were located predominantly within vacuoles of varying sizes in the cytoplasm of the macrophages and, occasionally, extracellularly within the intercellular spaces of the stroma.

nodes.description: Chronic scarring donovanosis can obstruct genital lymphatic drainage, producing genital lymphedema (elephantiasis), one of the recognized late complications of bacterial genital-ulcer STIs.

evidence.reference_title: Genital elephantiasis and sexually transmitted infections - revisited.
evidence.snippet: a small but significant proportion of patients develop genital elephantiasis due to bacterial sexually transmitted infections (STIs), mainly lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) and donovanosis.

nodes.description: Chronic lymphatic obstruction from long-standing donovanosis produces genital lymphedema (elephantiasis).

nodes.description: Donovanosis lesions are dominated by chronic granulomatous inflammation with macrophage-lineage histiocytes, neutrophils, and plasma cells. This persistent infiltrate supports granulation tissue and pseudoepitheliomatous epithelial reaction at the ulcer edge.

evidence.reference_title: Concomitant malacoplakia and granuloma inguinale of the cervix in acquired immune deficiency syndrome.
evidence.snippet: granulation tissue containing a dense plasma cell infiltrate, aggregates of neutrophils, and vacuolated enlarged histiocytes containing Donovan bodies were noted.
Other cells seen included plasma cells, polymorphonuclear cells and sparse lymphocytes.

nodes.description: Long-standing donovanosis lesions can undergo malignant transformation to squamous cell carcinoma.

evidence.reference_title: Malignant transformation of donovanosis (granuloma inguinale) in a HIV-positive patient.
evidence.snippet: In our case the patient did not respond to treatment for donovanosis and on biopsy we realized that the patient had coexistent SCC, which is hitherto unreported with granuloma inguinale.
